requirements.label: specialization
requirements.title: Advanced courses: required Specialization (choose one)

rules.label: Bioengineering
rules.manualCheck: Requires acceptance into the Bioengineering minor (BNG); priority goes to students with a 3.00 GPA or higher. The Bioengineering Specialization also requires calculus as MAT 125, MAT 126, MAT 127 OR MAT 131, MAT 132 OR AMS 151, AMS 161 (MAT 127 is the extra course on the MAT 125/126 route), and the Physics for Life Sciences sequence is not accepted. Complete one track (Biomaterials/Biomechanics with Calculus III; Bioelectricity with Linear Algebra; or Molecular/Cellular).
rules.sourceText: Bioengineering minor (BNG) tracks: Biomaterials/Biomechanics (BME 260, BME 303, and BME 353 or BME 381); Calculus III (AMS 261 or MAT 203); Bioelectricity (BME 271, BME 301, and BME 311 or BME 313 or BME 481); Linear Algebra (AMS 210 or MAT 211); Molecular/Cellular (BME 304, BME 381); PICK TWO of BME 404, BME 402, BME 371; One advanced biology lecture course; One advanced biology laboratory course. Student must be accepted into the Bioengineering minor.

rules.label: Developmental Genetics
rules.manualCheck: At least one of the two additional lecture courses must be from Area I, II or IV. Area restrictions (which advanced courses fall in Areas I-IV) are not part of the extracted catalog text and are not checked; confirm them with a Biology advisor. Advanced biology coursework must total at least 20 credits (standard program: 5 advanced BIO lecture and 2 advanced BIO laboratory courses); BIO 320 and BIO 321 cannot both count; research, readings, teaching practica and internships are not counted here.
rules.sourceText: Two additional advanced BIO lecture courses including at least one from Area I, Area II, or Area IV (or the listed other-department courses accepted in those areas); one additional advanced BIO laboratory course from any area; additional advanced BIO lecture, laboratory, reading, or independent research courses as needed for a minimum of 20 credits of advanced biology coursework.

rules.label: Ecology and Evolution
rules.manualCheck: One additional lecture and one laboratory from Area III or IV; two more lectures, at least one from Area I or II; one more laboratory from Area I, II or III. A 4-credit lecture-with-laboratory course may satisfy both a lecture and a laboratory requirement, but is counted once here. Area restrictions (which advanced courses fall in Areas I-IV) are not part of the extracted catalog text and are not checked; confirm them with a Biology advisor. Advanced biology coursework must total at least 20 credits (standard program: 5 advanced BIO lecture and 2 advanced BIO laboratory courses); BIO 320 and BIO 321 cannot both count; research, readings, teaching practica and internships are not counted here.
rules.sourceText: One additional advanced BIO lecture course and one advanced BIO laboratory course from Area III or Area IV (or listed other-department courses in those areas); two additional advanced BIO lecture courses including at least one from Area I or Area II; one advanced BIO laboratory course from Area I, II, or III; additional advanced BIO courses as needed for a minimum of 20 credits. A 4-credit Lecture with Laboratory course may satisfy both the lecture and lab requirement.

rules.label: Environmental Biology
rules.manualCheck: One laboratory and two additional courses from Area IV (at most one Environmental Biology course from another department); two more lectures, at least one from Area I or II; one laboratory from Area I, II or III. Area restrictions (which advanced courses fall in Areas I-IV) are not part of the extracted catalog text and are not checked; confirm them with a Biology advisor. Advanced biology coursework must total at least 20 credits (standard program: 5 advanced BIO lecture and 2 advanced BIO laboratory courses); BIO 320 and BIO 321 cannot both count; research, readings, teaching practica and internships are not counted here.
rules.sourceText: One advanced BIO laboratory course from Area IV (or listed other-department lab courses in that area); two additional advanced BIO courses from Area IV (at most one Environmental Biology course from other departments); two additional advanced BIO lecture courses including at least one from Area I or Area II; one advanced BIO laboratory course from Area I, II, or III; additional advanced BIO courses as needed for a minimum of 20 credits.

rules.label: Interdisciplinary Biology
rules.manualCheck: At least one lecture in each of Areas I, II, III and IV, a second lecture in one of those areas, and two laboratories from two different areas. Area restrictions (which advanced courses fall in Areas I-IV) are not part of the extracted catalog text and are not checked; confirm them with a Biology advisor. Advanced biology coursework must total at least 20 credits (standard program: 5 advanced BIO lecture and 2 advanced BIO laboratory courses); BIO 320 and BIO 321 cannot both count; research, readings, teaching practica and internships are not counted here.
rules.sourceText: At least one advanced BIO lecture course in each of Area I, Area II, Area III, and Area IV (or listed other-department courses in these areas); two advanced BIO laboratory courses from two different areas; a second advanced BIO lecture course in one of the four areas; additional advanced BIO courses as needed for a minimum of 20 credits.

requirements.sourceText: DECLARING A SPECIALIZATION IS REQUIRED TO COMPLETE THE BIOLOGY BS. The 7 Specializations are: Bioengineering, Developmental Genetics, Ecology and Evolution, Environmental Biology, Interdisciplinary Biology, Neuroscience, and Quantitative Biology and Bioinformatics.

requirements.label: upper-division-writing
requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: BIO 459 is a 0-credit course that must be co-registered with an approved advanced course from the list of courses that routinely offer BIO 459 assignments (BIO 312, 320, 321, 327, 335, 336, 344, 352, 353, 354, 356, 364, 365, 366, 367, 385, 386, EBH 302, EBH 380). A satisfactory writing sample must be submitted.

requirements.sourceText: Registration: students must co-register for the 0-credit BIO 459 course with an approved advanced course as listed below. To receive a satisfactory grade in BIO 459 and WRTD credit, either a lab report or term paper from the advanced course must be submitted prior to the end of the term.

policies.sourceText: All of these foundational courses in related fields must be taken for a letter grade; courses taken under the Pass/No Credit option will not count towards completion of the major, with the exception of the Spring 2020 semester.

All core and advanced courses in biology, including advanced courses in biology from other departments, must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of C or higher with the exception of 400 level Reading and Research courses that are graded on an S/U basis.

All core and advanced courses in biology, including advanced courses in biology from other departments, must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a grade of C or higher with the exception of 400 level Reading and Research courses that are graded on an S/U basis.
The organic chemistry lab must be passed with a C or higher.
A letter grade of D or higher is accepted towards the statistics requirement for the following courses: AMS 110, AMS 310, BIO 211, or EBH 230.

Transfer students must take at least 15 credits of required core and advanced biology at Stony Brook in courses for majors at the 200 level or higher. At least 12 of the 15 credits must be in BIO-designator courses. Both of the two advanced laboratory experiences must be taken at Stony Brook.

substitutions.condition: Students who transfer in AMS 102 from another institution with a grade of A or higher
substitutions.sourceText: Students who transfer in AMS 102 with a grade of A or higher receive credit for the statistics course.

fulfillment.sourceText: Satisfactory completion of BIO 459 will fulfill the Stony Brook Curriculum (SBC) "Write Effectively within One's Discipline (WRTD)" learning objectives.

notes.text: Students in the Biology BA or BS programs may not declare a double major among Biology, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Marine Sciences and Marine Vertebrate Biology. A double major in Biology and Human Evolutionary Biology requires a certain course combination in the Human Evolutionary Biology electives as specified in the EBH major.

Schedule advising appointments online through Navigate. Advisors: Rachel Pilero, Kayla McFadden, Allison Young. Office: Biology Learning Laboratories, Undergraduate Biology Office Suite, Rooms 104-112; (631) 632-8530.
Courses taken under the Pass/No Credit option will not count towards completion of the major, with the exception of the Spring 2020 semester.
Students must declare a Specialization to complete the Biology BS. Students may not take both BIO 320 and BIO 321 for major credit.

Bioengineering Specialization requires acceptance into the Bioengineering minor (BNG) by the College of Engineering and Applied Sciences; priority is given to students with a GPA of 3.00 or higher, and admission is competitive. The Physics for Life Sciences sequence is not accepted for this specialization.

AP Biology does not satisfy any Core Courses in Biology. AP statistics does not satisfy the BIO statistics requirement. Students who transfer in AMS 102 with a grade of A or higher receive credit for the statistics course.

Biology courses taken elsewhere apply only if listed as equivalent to a Stony Brook course in the official Transfer Course Database. Transfer students may satisfy related-field requirements with approved equivalent transfer courses.

Honors in Biology or Biology and Society requires a cumulative GPA of 3.50 or higher in major courses, a thesis based on at least two semesters of independent research (approved Research or Internship course, such as BIO 484, 486, 487, 488, or 489), and an Honors Application submitted to the Undergraduate Biology office by the second week of the last semester.

Students may pursue a special double major in Biology and Clinical Laboratory Sciences; speak with a Biology advisor. The Biology Secondary Teacher Education Program is listed under the Education and Teacher Certification entry.
Biology BA and the Biology Honors programs are separate from this BS requirement set. Accelerated and optional programs are not evaluated here.
Students responsible for DIV learning objective per Note 5 of the SBC table; SBC table lists courses that may fulfill SBC categories but per-course tags are not evaluated here.

Transfer students: at least 12 of the 15 Stony Brook credits must be in BIO-designator courses, and both advanced laboratory experiences must be taken at Stony Brook (the 15-credit minimum is checked; the BIO-designator and laboratory parts are not).

The major requires at least 70 credits including the chemistry, mathematics and physics foundation, and at least 20 credits of advanced biology coursework (standard program: 5 advanced BIO lecture courses and 2 advanced BIO laboratory courses). These totals are not checked as separate requirements. At least one semester of each two-semester sequence in calculus, organic chemistry lecture and physics must be passed with a C or higher (flagged for confirmation on those requirements).
